subject: general
question: The sign convention for focal length of a concave lens _________.
solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**is negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is a **diverging lens** that possesses at least one surface that curves inwards. It causes parallel beams of light to spread out or diverge after passing through it.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **optical center** of the lens is considered the **origin (0,0)**, and all distances are measured from this point.
 
• Distances measured in the **direction of incident light** are taken as **positive**, while those measured **opposite to the direction of incident light** are taken as **negative**.
 
• The **principal focus** of a **concave lens** is the point from which the rays of light, originally parallel to the axis, appear to diverge after passing through the lens. This point lies on the **same side** as the incident light (usually the **left side**).
 
• Because the distance from the **optical center** to the **principal focus** is measured against the direction of the incident light, the **focal length** of a **concave lens** is always **negative**. ***Hence, the statement that the sign convention is negative is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention for Convex Lens**:
 
 
• A **convex lens** is a **converging lens**. Its **principal focus** is located on the **opposite side** of the incident light (right side).
 
• Therefore, the **focal length** of a **convex lens** is always considered **positive** under the standard sign convention.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification**:
 
 
• The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the **lens formula**: **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• The **magnification (m)** produced by a lens is the ratio of image height to object height, which also equals **v/u**. For a **concave lens**, the magnification is always **positive** and **less than one**.
 
 
 
• **Power of a Lens**:
 
 
• The **power** of a lens is defined as the **reciprocal of its focal length** in meters (**P = 1/f**).
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. Since the focal length of a **concave lens** is **negative**, its **optical power** is also **negative**.
 
• For example, a person with **Myopia** (near-sightedness) is prescribed **concave lenses** with **negative power** (e.g., -2.5 D).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Image Formation by Concave Lens**:
 
 
• A **concave lens** always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**, regardless of where the object is placed in front of it.
 
• The **image distance (v)** for a **concave lens** is always **negative** because the image is formed on the same side as the object.
 
 
 
• **Object Distance (u)**:
 
 
• By convention, the **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens. Consequently, the **object distance (u)** is **always negative** in calculations for both convex and concave lenses.
